## Goal

Prevent ruff (the Python linter) from mis-parsing YAML and other non-Python configuration files as Python source, which produces false-positive `invalid-syntax` findings that pollute the Quality Improvement epic as auto-created work items. The fix MUST be **additive**: it must not hardcode any project-specific path (e.g. `proxy/config-cheap.yaml`), must not break scanning of other projects, and must never hide genuine Python findings in `.py` files in any project.

## Background / Root cause

The llm project Quality Improvement epic **LP-0MT1F4IQU00828FC** accumulated **155 false-positive child work items** (2026-08-20), all ruff `invalid-syntax` errors reported against `proxy/config-cheap.yaml` — a YAML file being linted as Python (Unexpected indentation, Invalid annotated assignment target, Expected an expression, etc.).

The existing explicit-file-argument filter (commit e910f02d, `_run_ruff_check` / `_run_ruff_fix_mode`) only excludes TS/JS extensions and only in the `files=` branch. Two gaps remain:
1. The **whole-project scan path** (`files=None`, the `else` branch) runs `ruff check <root>` with only a TS/JS `--extend-exclude` — it does NOT exclude `.yaml`/`.yml` or other non-Python config files.
2. The current exclusion list is English-agnostic about additivity — it must be extended to cover non-Python config extensions generically so the fix holds for ANY project (not just llm), while never suppressing genuine findings.

Related existing item: **SA-0MSTMAPL40019JX5** addresses the explicit-file-argument path in the audit runner. This item covers the whole-project scan path and generalises the exclusion so it is additive across all projects.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The whole-project ruff scan path (`files=None`) excludes non-Python configuration extensions (at minimum `.yaml`, `.yml`, `.json`, `.toml`, `.md`) so ruff never mis-parses them, via `--extend-exclude`/`--force-exclude` — not by hardcoding any project-specific filename.
2. Genuine ruff findings on `.py` files are unaffected: existing tests pass and no Python lint is suppressed.
3. The fix is additive — works for any project root (verified with a non-llm project containing a `.yaml` file), with no hardcoded absolute paths or project names in the exclusion logic.
4. A regression test asserts that scanning a project tree containing a `.yaml` file (both a whole-project scan and an explicit-file scan) produces zero findings for that YAML file, while a `.py` file with a genuine issue still yields its finding.
5. The change is documented in the linter_runner module docstring/comment (both the explicit-file and whole-project paths).
data.title: Ruff: exclude YAML & non-Python files additively across all projects (whole-project scan)

data.description:
## Summary

While shipping LLM-proxy v0.1.19, the ship wrapper was invoked with an unrecognised flag (to read help). It **ran the entire post-release sequence without performing a release**, closing 74 real release-candidate work items with the previous release's reason (`Shipped in v0.1.18`). The real release then found zero candidates and produced an empty changelog. Full incident: llm worklog **LP-0MUEALIM60037F1S**.

## Root cause

1. **No argument validation in `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js`.** Only `--skip-checks` is wrapper-only; every other flag (including `--help`) is forwarded to `merge-dev-to-main.sh`.
2. **`merge-dev-to-main.sh` treats `-h|--help` as usage and `exit 0`** — so the child succeeds without releasing.
3. **`runReleaseImpl` does not detect the no-op release.** It skips the PR wait (no PR URL), runs a no-op `syncDevWithMain()`, then resolves `version` from `git describe --tags --abbrev=0` — the **previous** tag.
4. **`verifyReleaseMerge(version)` only checks** that the tag exists on `origin` and is an ancestor of `origin/main`. The previous tag already satisfies this, so the guard passes.
5. **`closeWorkItemsAfterRelease(version)` then closes every `stage=in_review` item with the wrong reason.**

## Overlap resolution (duplicate check, Step 4.3)

Steps 1–4 and 5's *close* trigger were fixed by the overlapping, now-completed
work item **SA-0MV0PZYMI004SUFR** ("ship: run-release.js --help runs
post-release steps and closes items against a stale tag") and its children
SA-0MV13B5F8005NT6G (fail-fast CLI), SA-0MV13B5WO008CYXA (newly-created-tag
gate) and SA-0MV13B4YT0093CKT (regression tests). Verified in the current tree:

- `parseReleaseArgs()` + `runRelease()` reject unknown flags (exit 13) and make
  `--help`/`-h` fully inert (usage, exit 0) before the Code Freeze marker or any
  gate runs.
- `snapshotReleaseTags()` / `isNewlyCreatedTag()` gate every post-release step:
  a tag that already existed before the run exits 14 without closing anything.

The remaining, still-unmet gap from the original criteria is **idempotency of
the close sweep**: `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease()` unconditionally re-issues
`wl close --reason "Shipped in v<version>"` for every candidate, so a repeated
post-release run (or an item already annotated for this version by an earlier
sweep) is re-closed and re-annotated — the 99 spurious close comments / 25
double-closed items observed in the incident. This work item now covers that
gap only.

## Desired behaviour / Acceptance Criteria (remaining gap)

- [ ] AC1: `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease(version)` skips any candidate that already carries a close marker for **this** version (`Shipped in v<version>`), with **no** `wl close` and **no** additional comment/annotation for that item; the skipped items are reported in the return value.
- [ ] AC2: The marker match is version-exact — `Shipped in v0.1.1` must not match version `0.1.18` (and vice versa); markers for other versions do not suppress a close.
- [ ] AC3: Reading the existing markers is injectable/fail-safe: an unreadable comment source logs a warning and leaves the existing close behaviour intact (a release is never blocked by the idempotency check); no test touches the live worklog.
- [ ] AC4: Regression tests cover (a) a re-run of the post-release close does not duplicate `wl close` calls or comments, (b) an item carrying another version's marker is still closed, (c) version-exact matching, (d) the unreadable-marker fail-safe path.
- [ ] AC5: Full test suite passes; `skill/ship/SKILL.md` / reference docs describe the idempotency guarantee.

## Key files

- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease` (marker check), new pure helper for version-exact marker detection.
- `tests/unit/test-close-work-items-after-release.mjs` — regression tests.
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` / `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — documentation.

## Already delivered by SA-0MV0PZYMI004SUFR (not re-implemented here)

- `--help`/`-h` inert; unknown flags rejected non-zero before any post-release step.
- `verifyReleaseMerge` alone is insufficient — a newly-created-tag gate now
  proves *this* run produced the release tag.
- Post-release close/notify/cleanup skipped whenever no new tag was created.
data.title: run-release.js runs post-release steps without a release: unknown flags forwarded, verifyReleaseMerge accepts the previous tag

# Audit runner: parent-persisted child audits demote snapshot-exempt children

**Discovered-from:** WL-0MVFNMSRW002FI6B (ContextHub) — canonicalised here because this repository owns the audit skill.
**Issue type:** bug · **Priority:** high · **Recurrence of:** SA-0MUJAPC680078396 (completed) and SA-0MSGMR7CX00588TZ (completed)
**RCA:** `docs/dev/audit-child-demotion-rca.md`

## Problem statement

A parent audit running in **separate-process child mode** (`--no-child-in-main-slot`) demoted **all 11** of its children from `completed`/`in_review` to `open`/`blocked` at `plan_complete`, at the exact timestamps their child audits were persisted. F1 and F8 (the two dependency-free children) were set to `open`; the other nine cascaded to `blocked` through the dependency chain. The parent's own verdict then read `Ready to close: No` with the sole blocker being those now-`plan_complete` children, even though all six of its own acceptance criteria were `met`/`adjusted`.

This is the side-effect demotion that SA-0MUJAPC680078396 explicitly forbids and that SA-0MSGMR7CX00588TZ was meant to prevent ('infra-fallback verdicts must never demote').

## Root cause (proven)

`_persist_child_audit()` persists child audits through `persist_audit.py`, which calls:

    wl audit-set <child> --ready-to-close no

and `wl audit-set` with a negative verdict calls `db.revertToPlanComplete(child)` (`src/commands/audit-result.ts:207-214`; `packages/shared` `database.revertToPlanComplete`), which unconditionally rewrites `completed`/`in_review` → `open`/`plan_complete`.

Two invariants are therefore bypassed:

1. **The audited item's lifecycle guards.** `ac_fallback_used` (SA-0MSGMR7CX00588TZ) and `_cascade_suppress_demotion` (SA-0MUJAPC680078396) live in `_apply_terminal_lifecycle` for the *item under audit*. `persist_audit` → `audit-set` is a skill-unaware primitive and consults neither.
2. **The child-exemption snapshot.** `_child_is_exempt` is only consulted by the runner's own closure checks, not by `audit-set`.

Measured: 8 of 11 children were persisted with `readyToClose=false` (`wl audit-show --json`) and every one was reverted; the 3 with `true` were not. Dependency cascade then produced the 9 `blocked` states.

**Aggravating factor.** Those child verdicts were infra-fallback-tainted: `AUDIT_RELIABILITY_SUMMARY calls=27 parse_ok=20 parse_failed=7 timeouts=7`, with 5 of 11 child Phase-1 screens landing exactly on the 600 s `AUDIT_CHILD_SCREEN_TIMEOUT` cap. Per SA-0MSGMR7CX00588TZ an infra-fallback 'No' is not an explicit model assessment and must take the **restore** path — but `audit-set` has no notion of fallback provenance, so tainted verdicts demote.

**Open sub-question (to confirm in this item).** The parent's closure reported those children as blocking even though they were `in_review` at audit start and `_capture_exempt_children_snapshot` should have exempted them. `all_children_reviewed` honours `snapshot_exempt` (audit_runner.py ~5633) but the report's `not_reviewed` text path (~5759) does **not**, so text and verdict can disagree. Determine whether the snapshot was empty (children already demoted pre-snapshot), lost, or simply not applied to the text path.

## User stories

- **Audit operator** — As an operator, I want a parent audit to leave the lifecycle of children that were `in_review` at audit start untouched, so a read-only run never pushes completed work back into the actionable queue.
- **Release manager** — As a release manager, I want `blocked` never to cascade through a dependency chain as a side effect of an audit, so a release gate cannot be stalled by an audit artefact.
- **Maintainer** — As a maintainer, I want infra-fallback child verdicts to be recorded as `partial` diagnostics, never as lifecycle-changing 'No's.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A child audit persisted by a parent run (both child-audit modes) **cannot** change a child's status/stage when the child was `completed`/`in_review` at audit start: `_persist_child_audit`/`persist_audit` either writes the audit without the `audit-set` reversion side effect, or the runner restores the captured pre-audit status/stage immediately after persisting.
2. Infra-fallback-tainted child verdicts (parse failure, timeout, provider error, concurrency limit) never demote any item — the same rule SA-0MSGMR7CX00588TZ applies to the audited item now applies to children persisted by a parent.
3. No `blocked` status may be introduced on any work item as a side effect of an audit run; verified by a regression test asserting the full child set's status/stage is byte-identical before and after a parent audit.
4. The parent's closure decision and its report text use the **same** exemption source: `not_reviewed` (~5759) honours `snapshot_exempt`, so a parent whose children were all `in_review` at audit start reports `Ready to close: Yes` when its own ACs pass.
5. A regression test covers the observed scenario end to end (parent + N children, all `in_review`, child verdicts `No` and tainted): children end `completed`/`in_review`, parent verdict `Yes`, no `blocked`.
6. `skill/audit/tests/` passes, including the new tests.

## Evidence

ContextHub run log: `~/.audit_debug/ContextHub/audit-WL-0MVFNMSRW002FI6B-2nd-20261021-102346.log` (9312 s; `AUDIT_RELIABILITY_SUMMARY calls=27 parse_ok=20 parse_failed=7 timeouts=7`). Child `readyToClose` values and the pre/post lifecycle states are reproducible from the child items under `WL-0MVFNMSRW002FI6B`.
data.title: Audit runner: parent-persisted child audits demote snapshot-exempt in_review children (recurrence of SA-0MUJAPC680078396)

data.comment:
Implementation complete, pushed to dev at commit 7153465b8.

Summary:
- Added module-level RUFF_NON_PYTHON_EXCLUDE (globs for .ts/.tsx/.js/.jsx/.mjs/.cjs + .yaml/.yml/.json/.toml/.md) and PYTHON_SOURCE_EXTENSIONS to skill/code_review/scripts/linter_runner.py and mirrored in skill/code-review/scripts/linter_runner.py.
- Both ruff paths now exclude non-Python extensions via --extend-exclude + --force-exclude: whole-project scan (files=None) and explicit-file scope (files=[...], already filtered to .py).
- Additive/project-agnostic: pure **/*.<ext> globs, no project names or absolute paths (AC3).
- Regression tests in tests/test_linter_runner_non_python_exclude.py (12 tests): command construction for both scan paths (check + fix/rescan), both module copies, and behavioural real-ruff tests (project with include=['*.py','*.yaml'] + yaml files + genuine .py issues → zero yaml findings in whole-project AND explicit-file scans; .py findings preserved). 59 changed-scope tests green; full suite green at dev-push gate.
- Docs: module docstring + function docstrings document the exclusion for both paths (AC5).

Related gap noted (not changed): skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py _build_ruff_fix_cmd keeps a TS-only --extend-exclude but its callers pre-filter files to .py, so behaviour is equivalent; could adopt the shared constant if refactored.
